source.title: DVERGE: Diversifying Vulnerabilities for Enhanced Robust Generation of Ensembles
source.authors: Huan-Rui Yang; Jingyang Zhang; Hongliang Dong; Nathan Inkawhich; Andrew B. Gardner; Andrew Touchet; Wesley Wilkes; Heath Berry; H. Li

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results on adversarial-vulnerability overlap and transfer between ensemble members, not on the representation-alignment or convergence measures named in the claim versions. Its statements about independently trained models learning similar non-robust features are background attributed to prior work.
record.gate_note: The paper measures vulnerability diversity and adversarial transferability, which are related to but distinct from the claim's representation-alignment measures. The paper's own results on those measures are recorded with versions ["none"] below. Cited findings are not recorded as rows. Robustness accuracy results are omitted because they do not measure representation convergence.
record.test_reason: DVERGE is an ensemble-defence method. It takes as a premise, from cited work (Ilyas et al.; Li et al. convergent learning), that independently trained CNNs share non-robust features. It then deliberately trains sub-models to diverge and reports its own method's transferability and robustness. It never measures representation alignment, so it tests no version. Its own measures (vulnerability diversity, adversarial transfer) are a related but different construct. The record's T6/discusses undersells the reliance on the shared-feature premise.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. DVERGE distills non-robust features to diversify sub-model vulnerabilities, cutting within-ensemble transfer from over 60% to under 6%. This raises black-box and white-box ensemble robustness with small clean-accuracy loss, and combines with adversarial training.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses feature distillation and adversarial transferability to diversify vulnerabilities in CIFAR-10 CNN ensembles; it does not measure cross-model representation alignment or convergence with scale.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported vulnerability diversity and transferability vary with training epsilon, ensemble size, and the layer used for distillation; shallow versus deep distillation layers also change the robustness outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard-trained ResNet-20 ensembles on CIFAR-10 share adversarial vulnerability. Figure 1 shows sub-models vulnerable along the same transfer axis. Hold-out baseline-ensemble attacks drive baseline black-box accuracy to 0% at eps 0.03 (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained same-architecture CNNs on the same dataset share adversarial vulnerabilities, so attacks transfer between them.

fits_no_version.finding: DVERGE training raises vulnerability diversity and cuts within-ensemble transfer to 3-6%, versus 60-70% for ADP and over 80% for one GAL pair. Some pairs in 5-sub-model ensembles stay highly transferable (79%/48%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared vulnerability between ensemble members can be largely removed by training on each other's distilled non-robust features, though not uniformly across pairs.

record.problems: The paper does not test the claim's representation-alignment outcomes. Its relevant measurements concern adversarial vulnerability and transferability, so they cannot establish whether representations converge. Several outcomes are presented in figures without numerical values in the text; the paper reports averages over three runs for robustness evaluations but does not give uncertainty for the diversity and transferability values recorded here.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; the recorded rows are the textually stated vulnerability-diversity and transferability results relevant as related findings. Other robustness-accuracy tables and plots were left out because they do not measure representation convergence or vulnerability overlap directly.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep and no alignment measure.
No shared-feature or subspace measurement across seeds; only adversarial transfer between standard-trained ResNet-20s.
No interpretable feature or circuit matching.
No variation of similarity metric or inputs for alignment.
No assessment of alignment level or its causes.

missing.what: Baseline (standard-trained) ensemble pairwise transferability and decision-region overlap. This is the only result showing shared vulnerability among independently trained models, and it is shown in figures only.
missing.locator: Figure 1, Figure 3 baseline panel, Figure 7; Table 4 baseline rows

record.verdict_notes: Convergent learning (arXiv:1511.07543) is cited only as reference [7], as background for shared vulnerability. Every recorded row concerns adversarial transfer or method tuning, so all stay at versions ['none'] and no verdict labels are given.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of model size or capability, and no measurement of representation alignment across differently trained models.
No paired image-caption or vision-language models.
The paper does not measure shared features or subspaces across random initializations.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
The paper varies settings for adversarial feature distillation and attacks, not similarity-measure settings or input distributions for representation alignment.
The paper does not assess whether representation alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives explain such alignment.
